task: Each source has two targets: finite2 with new response parameters, or recurrent with the original response parameters. Both targets share paid prefix controls. Private family labels and seeds appear only in the experiment protocol/results.
source: The first actual published archive supplies author practice. The remaining two published archives supply transfer; their files are loaded only after authoring stops. Preserve the earlier unsuccessful acquisition and its costs separately.
intervention: Luna writes, practices and publishes select_actions on three anonymous cases. The seed only checks the old predictor; the fixed DEFAULT procedure is not supplied to the author. Transfer compares its frozen published source with the existing developer-authored DEFAULT_RESEARCH_PROCEDURE on identical evidence.
controller: The author selects program edits, paid practice and publication. Each practice and transfer begins with 72 paid controls-only rows, then executes at most 12 declared program steps with 24-row fresh confirmation. All fits and observations share each episode's actual budgets. Transfer uses zero LLM calls; this is LLM-authored method execution, not online LLM selection of each action.
archive_publication: New predictors retain ordinary code, data and binary dependencies. Imported confirmed-model archives accompany them only when declared in the successful finish.reused_files. Runner logs and the undeclared candidate catalog are excluded. An unchanged directly submitted archive keeps its existing dependencies. Revisions to an inherited model publish a new candidate. A latest predictor explicitly depending on an older candidate retains that dependency, which is reported.
failure_policy: This explicitly requested additional development phase retains all prior failures. No automatic retry or unpublished-source transfer follows. If publication fails, preserve the six learned slots as skipped and run fixed cases only as resource references.
accounting: Report old source acquisition, new author/practice and zero-LLM transfer costs separately. Charge each paid prefix in its own practice/transfer episode. The actual run total adds the author once and all executed targets; unknown provider usage remains null. Program steps are not provider calls.
terminal_order: Publish using paid practice and fresh confirmation only. Freeze the method before loading transfer archives. Complete all transfer research before terminal scoring; no terminal outcome affects publication or target admission.
scope: Two previously learned apparatus realizations, each tested under unchanged, response-parameter and recurrent-instrument conditions: six paired targets. New preregistered trajectory and changed-response seeds avoid replaying the old six targets. This is cross-source transfer within existing apparatus families, not new-apparatus or open-world discovery.
model_identity: gpt-6-luna is requested through the existing subscription provider. Usage metadata repeating that name does not independently establish server routing.

continue_author.restoration: Keep the exact current source, paid trial files and source-specific coverage. Cases, archives, base seeds, confirmation streams and thresholds are unchanged. Previously paid trials are not rerun during restoration. Source edits require fresh confirmation of every case with that edited source before publication.
continue_author.budget: This is an explicitly added development allowance after budget exhaustion, not success within the original author budget. Old actual costs remain cumulative; they are not subtracted again from this new allowance. Cumulative limits equal prior actual costs plus this allowance, using known tokens only and disclosing unknown usage.
continue_author.evidence: Only prior author practice and public interfaces enter the author context. Previous fixed-reference and transfer outcomes remain excluded. Continued authoring and the unchanged transfer targets are development evidence, not independent authoring.
continue_author.transfer: After authoring stops, execute the registered targets afresh. Retain all earlier fixed-reference costs separately.
